component.name: milo-server
component.title: OPC UA Server
component.description: Expose values as variable nodes of an embedded OPC UA server, which OPC UA clients can read and write.
component.label: iot

applicationName.description: The application name of the server. If not set, Apache Camel Milo Server is used.

applicationUri.description: The application URI of the server. If not set, urn:org:apache:camel:milo:server is used.

bindAddresses.description: A comma-separated list of the local addresses that the server binds to. If not set, it binds to localhost. For each address, the server has endpoints for the host name of the machine and for the host names of that address.

buildInfo.description: The build information of the server, as an org.eclipse.milo.opcua.stack.core.types.structured.BuildInfo, which clients can read from the Server object.

namespaceUri.description: The URI of the namespace that holds the items of the milo-server endpoints. A client addresses an item with this URI and the item ID, for example nsu=urn:org:apache:camel;s=myItem.

path.description: The path of the endpoint URLs of the server, after the host and the port. It does not need to start with a slash. The discovery endpoint always has the path /discovery.

port.description: The TCP port that the server listens on.

productUri.description: The product URI of the server. If not set, urn:org:apache:camel:milo is used.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

certificate.label: security
certificate.description: The certificate of the server, as a java.security.cert.X509Certificate, which the endpoints of the server announce.

certificateManager.label: security
certificateManager.description: To use a custom org.eclipse.milo.opcua.stack.core.security.CertificateManager that holds the certificate and the key pair of the server. Not used when defaultCertificateValidator is set. When certificateValidator is set, the certificate groups of this certificate manager validate the certificates of the clients with that validator.

certificateValidator.label: security
certificateValidator.description: To use a custom org.eclipse.milo.opcua.stack.core.security.CertificateValidator that validates the certificates of the OPC UA clients, instead of the validators of the certificate groups of certificateManager. Requires certificateManager, which holds the certificate of the server. Cannot be used together with defaultCertificateValidator.

defaultCertificateValidator.label: security
defaultCertificateValidator.description: The directory of a file based trust list for the certificates of the OPC UA clients, in the layout used by Eclipse Milo: trusted certificates in trusted/certs, their CRLs in trusted/crl, certificates of issuing CAs in issuer/certs and their CRLs in issuer/crl. Rejected certificates are put in rejected/certs. The directories are created if they do not exist.

enableAnonymousAuthentication.label: security
enableAnonymousAuthentication.description: Whether the endpoints of the server offer the Anonymous user token policy, for clients that connect without a user name.

securityPolicies.label: security
securityPolicies.description: The security policies of the endpoints of the server, as a Set of org.eclipse.milo.opcua.stack.core.security.SecurityPolicy. Only None and Basic256Sha256 create endpoints, Basic256Sha256 with the security mode SignAndEncrypt. If neither this option nor securityPoliciesById is set, the endpoints use None.

securityPoliciesById.label: security
securityPoliciesById.description: A comma-separated list of the security policies of the endpoints of the server, as URIs or as names of org.eclipse.milo.opcua.stack.core.security.SecurityPolicy. They are added to the securityPolicies option. Only None and Basic256Sha256 create endpoints.

userAuthenticationCredentials.label: security
userAuthenticationCredentials.description: The users that the server accepts, as comma-separated user:password pairs, for example user1:pwd1,user2:pwd2. The user names and passwords are URL decoded: URL encode a comma, a percent sign or a plus sign in them, and a colon in a user name.

usernameSecurityPolicyUri.label: security
usernameSecurityPolicyUri.description: The security policy of the UserName user token policy, which the client uses to encrypt the password, as a name of org.eclipse.milo.opcua.stack.core.security.SecurityPolicy. If not set, Basic256Sha256 is used. Only used when userAuthenticationCredentials is set.

consumerOut.description: The Milo DataValue an OPC UA client wrote to the item: its getValue().getValue() is the value

producerIn.description: The new value of the item: an OPC UA built-in value such as a String, a number, a boolean, a Variant or a DataValue. Another object, such as a Map or a stream, is accepted but clients cannot read it

itemId.description: The ID of the item: the string node ID of a variable node in the namespace of the namespaceUri option. A client addresses the item myItem in the default namespace as nsu=urn:org:apache:camel;s=myItem. The consumer receives the values that clients write to the node, and the producer sets its value.

Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.
